title: Tapioca Pudding
subtitle: Pearl tapioca simmered in sweetened milk until soft and translucent
excerpt: Small cassava pearls soaked in cold water, then simmered in sweetened milk until completely soft and translucent, giving a silky pudding with a characteristic gentle bounce to each pearl.
sourceNotes: Tapioca pudding was a staple British nursery and school pudding through the 20th century, made from the dried starch pearls of the cassava root. Mrs Beeton and Eliza Acton both include milk puddings of this type. It acquired a bad reputation from decades of school canteen cooking where it was served lukewarm and over-thickened; properly made, it is considerably more delicate.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Can be made up to 4 hours ahead and served at room temperature or chilled.

content.text: Tapioca pudding is small cassava pearls cooked slowly in sweetened milk until each pearl becomes completely translucent and the milk thickens around them to a silky, gently cohesive pudding. The soak in cold water beforehand is important: it begins to hydrate the starch and brings the cooking time down considerably. Without soaking, the pearls take 40 minutes or more and tend to cook unevenly.
Place the tapioca pearls in a bowl and cover with cold water. Leave to soak for 30 minutes. The pearls will swell slightly and turn from opaque white to a faintly translucent grey. Drain and rinse.

Combine the drained tapioca, milk, and sugar in a medium saucepan. Bring slowly to a gentle simmer over a medium-low heat, stirring frequently. Once simmering, reduce to the lowest heat and cook for 20 to 25 minutes, stirring every few minutes to stop the tapioca settling and sticking to the base. The pudding is ready when every pearl is completely translucent, no white centre remaining, and the pudding has thickened to a consistency that coats the back of a spoon.

Remove from the heat. Stir in the vanilla extract and the cream if using. Pour into bowls and serve warm. The pudding will thicken as it cools, if serving cold, stir in an extra splash of milk before refrigerating and stir again before serving.

items.symptom: The pearls still have an opaque white centre after 25 minutes
items.cause: The heat was too low, or the soaking step was skipped.
items.fix: Continue cooking over a gentle simmer, stirring regularly. Add a splash more milk if the pudding is thickening before the pearls are cooked through.

items.symptom: The pudding is solid when cold
items.cause: Tapioca thickens dramatically as it cools, this is normal.
items.fix: Stir in a generous splash of cold milk before refrigerating. When serving cold, stir again and add more milk to loosen to the desired consistency.

items.symptom: The tapioca has lumped together into a mass
items.cause: The heat was too high, or stirring was infrequent.
items.fix: Cook at a gentle simmer and stir more frequently. A heavy-based pan helps even heat distribution.

content.text: Keeps in the fridge for 2 days, covered. Stir in a splash of cold milk before serving from cold, as the pudding sets quite firmly in the fridge. Reheat gently in a pan with a little milk, stirring constantly, until warm through.
